newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish share index and volume at new record.
newsitem.headline: Turkish share index and volume at new record.

text.p: Istanbul shares surged to the year's 16th record close on Friday in a continued rally amid heavy turnover boosted by strong liquidity influx, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 closed at an all-time high of 1,503, up 151 points, or 11.17 percent from Thursday's previous record of 1,352. In dollar terms, it stood at a new record of 1.3 cents, up from yesterday's 1.18 cents.
Daily volume also soared to a record of 64.87 trillion lira ($564.1 million) from Thursday's previous high of 43.46 trillion ($377.9 million).

The index's non-stop gains have totalled 54 percent so far this year. In dollar terms, it jumped by almost 43 percent since end-1996. Last year, the index had risen 143.8 percent and 35.8 percent in dollar terms.

"Participation has increased sharply. I expect small investors to step into the market as well after seeing the current gains. The uptrend remains intact and the market looks strong," said Huseyin Istanbullu from Meksa securities.
He said purchases by brokerages known to work with foreign investors were seen in several shares.

The latest uptrend was further fuelled by the constitutional court's Thursday rejection of a challenge to a law enabling the privatisation of Turk Telekom, the centrepiece of the government's 1997 sell-off programme.
Positive sentiment and liquidity influx triggered by the court's decision have pulled the index up 252 points, or 20.1 percent since Wednesday's record closing of 1,251.
